meta.scene_summary: We're busy building the future with trillion-dollar models while our local files and private data are being held hostage by the weather report.

cooking.headline: OpenAI raised $11B, proving that 'missing expectations' is just a fun way to say 'trillionaire'
cooking.summary: OpenAI just raised a massive round at a $1.25 trillion valuation despite missing their own $1.4 trillion target. It turns out that when you lose a couple hundred billion in expected value, you still end up with enough cash to buy a small country.
cooking.plain_english: OpenAI secured 11 billion dollars in funding, reaching a total company valuation of 1.25 trillion dollars.

cooking.headline: Anthropic is now building its own power plants because the cloud isn't just code anymore
cooking.summary: Anthropic signed a multi-billion dollar deal to secure gas-fired power specifically for their data centers. We've officially moved from optimizing code to becoming the utility company we were trying to avoid.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic has entered a 3.4 billion dollar agreement to ensure a dedicated supply of electricity from natural gas for its data centers.

cooking.headline: Apple wants Siri to stop being a glorified kitchen timer and actually do something.
cooking.summary: Apple is pushing for a more ambitious AI strategy because Siri currently has the decision-making skills of a brick. It turns out that when your virtual assistant can't set a reminder without a prompt, it's time for a major software architecture overhaul.
cooking.plain_english: Apple is pressuring its software team to develop more advanced artificial intelligence capabilities for Siri.

cooking.headline: Running a 284B model on 64GB of RAM is just glorified swap space abuse
cooking.summary: Someone figured out how to cram a massive model into a consumer laptop using pure audacity and probably a lot of patience. It's the computational equivalent of trying to fit a semi-truck through a drive-thru window.
cooking.plain_english: A developer created a method to run a very large artificial intelligence model on a standard computer with limited memory by optimizing how the data is processed.

cooking.headline: Maple makes 6GB GPUs feel like high-end hardware again
cooking.summary: Maple lets you squeeze a 26B parameter model onto a budget card that usually struggles to load a browser tab. It's the closest thing to a tech miracle until you realize your GPU is currently screaming for mercy while running it.
cooking.plain_english: A new software tool allows large artificial intelligence models to run on lower-cost graphics cards by reducing the amount of data required to process information.

cooked.headline: Claude Code's 'Don't Ask Again' button is just a shortcut to your secret keys
cooked.summary: Anthropic built a feature to remove friction from coding, but it accidentally turned your public GitHub repo into a shared password manager. It turns out that when you tell an AI to never ask for permission again, it interprets that as a license to commit your .env file to production.
cooked.plain_english: A coding assistant tool by Anthropic caused users to accidentally upload sensitive credentials to public GitHub repositories because of a feature that automatically bypassed confirmation prompts.

cooked.headline: A $133 million French bank heist proves your vendor is your weakest link
cooked.summary: The hackers didn't break into the bank's vault; they just compromised a third-party service provider that had the keys to the kingdom. It is the digital equivalent of hiring a locksmith who keeps a spare key taped to the outside of your front door.
cooked.plain_english: Cybercriminals stole 133 million dollars from a French bank by gaining unauthorized access to the bank's systems through a compromised third-party service provider.

cooked.headline: Microsoft removed local PC migration so you can pay them to store your files in the cloud.
cooked.summary: Microsoft is sunsetting direct PC-to-PC migration, effectively turning your data transfer into a mandatory OneDrive subscription side quest. It is the digital equivalent of a landlord removing the front door and charging you rent for the key to the new one.
cooked.plain_english: Microsoft has removed the built-in tool for transferring files between two computers, forcing users to rely on OneDrive for backups.

cooked.headline: Your free weather app is basically a private investigator with a data plan
cooked.summary: Police are buying location data from ad-tech brokers because getting a warrant is apparently too much paperwork. It turns out the biggest threat to your privacy isn't a hacker, but the 'Terms of Service' you clicked accept on to play Candy Crush.
cooked.plain_english: Law enforcement agencies are purchasing location data collected by mobile advertising networks to track individuals without obtaining a court warrant.

cooked.headline: GitHub is down, so I guess it's a forced productivity day
cooked.summary: GitHub going down is the universal sign to either start actually working or take a very long lunch break. It's funny how our entire industry effectively enters a state of suspended animation the moment the green contribution squares stop updating.
cooked.plain_english: The website used by developers to store and collaborate on code is currently experiencing a service outage.
